ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your request to reverse the SGD 4.00 cancellation charge is not supported by the record, and the driver is entitled to compensation. To the driver: the fee stands and you are paid under POL-NS-07.

ARRIVAL. POL-NS-01(a) is met — the trip record EV-TRIP-09101 logs a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-01T08:10:20+08:00 and the driver ended the trip. On limb (b) and POL-NS-02, EV-GPS-09101 places the driver 24.01 m from the pickup pin on all 33 fixes (min = mean = max), well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage and zero gaps; 33 qualifying consecutive in-radius fixes far exceed the three POL-NS-02 requires, and the trace opens at 08:10:00, twenty seconds before the arrival tap. POL-NS-05 does not fire: at the arrival timestamp the driver was stationary (single distinct speed 0.0 kph) 24 m from the pin — neither more than 300 m away nor travelling at 15 kph or above — so the marker is true and the waiting clock is not recomputed.

DWELL. Limb (c) is met. The one qualifying in-geofence run lasts 320 seconds, from the first qualifying fix at 08:10:00 to the 08:15:20 cancellation, against the 300-second STANDARD minimum — a 20-second surplus (derived shortfall of MINUS 20 seconds). Limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying GPS fix, not from the tap, so the surplus holds on the clause's own arithmetic. There is no second in-geofence interval to sum, so the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09101-01 (MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) is not required by anyone and POL-NS-06 is not engaged. Limb (d) is met: the trip was terminated by the driver at 08:15:20 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) recognises, with no boarding event.

THE RIDER'S ROUTES DO NOT FIRE. POL-NS-04 fails at limb (a): EV-CHAT-09101 holds three messages — the system 'Your driver has arrived' notice at 08:10:21 and two driver messages at 08:10:35 and 08:14:10 — and no rider locating or coordinating message, so the clause cannot exonerate you regardless of the reply interval or of rider presence. Independently, the rider track in EV-GPS-09101 carries 15 fixes all at 519.37 m from the pin (rider_qualifying_fix_count 0 of 15), far outside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius, so limb (c) places you nowhere near the pickup on your own device; the account that you were 'downstairs' is not borne out by the record. POL-NS-03 does not apply because the driver's fixes sit inside the arrival radius, not at a wrong face of the venue within the 400 m ceiling. POL-NS-06 does not apply because there was no shortfall.

MONEY. The SGD 4.00 fee is the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00); the two dimensions agree, the fare breakdown difference reads 0.00, and no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect arises. Under POL-NS-07 the driver is compensated at 80 per cent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee — SGD 3.20 — with SGD 0.80 retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, so the second limb is never reached and compensation is not withheld.

NO ESCALATION. No POL-NS-09 trigger applies: no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or presence; rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0 (limb (c)); rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 (limb (d)); the anti-farming check does not trip; and no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence (limb (e)). The deciding facts are carried by clean weight-1.0 artifacts (EV-GPS-09101, EV-TRIP-09101, EV-FARE-09101), so confidence sits at 0.90, above the 0.70 floor.

DISPOSITION. On the charge itself the present state stands — fare_breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — but because the case produces a driver payment the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and per POL-GEN-03 amount_sgd carries the same SGD 3.20 as driver_compensation_sgd.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both parties have, in the end, done the same arithmetic, and the record supports it. This is a rider-filed dispute over the SGD 6.00 cancellation fee charged on TRP-09102, and the question is whether the driver earned it under POL-NS-01.

All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold on this trip's own admissible evidence. (a) The trip record carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 22:40:20. (b) The GPS trace places the driver 24.0 m from the pickup pin (derived driver_track.max_distance_m 24.01 m over 51 qualifying fixes) at and before that timestamp, well inside the 150 m arrival radius the fee schedule sets for the AIRPORT zone class, and the qualifying run starts at 22:40:00, before the 'arrived' tap. (c) The continuous in-geofence dwell runs from the first qualifying fix at 22:40:00 to cancellation at 22:48:20, which is 500 seconds against the 480-second AIRPORT minimum - a surplus of 20 seconds, and the clock is run from the first in-geofence fix, not from the 'arrived' event, exactly as limb (c) requires. (d) The trip shows no boarding event and was terminated by the driver at 22:48:20, twenty seconds after the required dwell elapsed, on cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) recognises.

No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces the charge, and I answer each route the advocates raised. POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance) does not engage: it governs only a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m, whereas here the driver was 24.0 m from the pin, inside the radius. POL-NS-04 (rider contact unanswered) fails at limb (b): the rider wrote 'I am walking over now' at 22:41:40 and the driver replied 'Okay, I will remain at Door 5' at 22:41:58, eighteen seconds later, inside the 120-second window, so the clause does not apply whatever the reply said. Limb (c) also fails affirmatively on the rider's own track - 519.47 m from the pin on its 24 fixes, with 0 qualifying fixes inside the 200 m AIRPORT rider-presence radius - but limb (b) alone closes this route. POL-NS-05 (false arrival marker) does not engage: matched to the 22:40:20 event the driver sat 24.0 m from the pin at 0.0 km/h, far inside the 300 m distance threshold and below the 15 km/h motion threshold, so no waiting clock is recomputed. POL-NS-06 (waiting-period shortfall) does not engage: the 500-second run against the 480-second minimum leaves a shortfall of -20.0 seconds, that is, no shortfall at all, and the trace shows a single in-geofence interval with no excursions, so the limb (i) accumulation question is never reached.

On the money: POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the SGD 6.00 cancellation fee itemised in the fare breakdown, which is SGD 4.80 (80 percent of SGD 6.00), the residual SGD 1.20 being the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not bite - driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the four-termination limb, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d 120 is 0.008, below the 0.08 rate limb, and the clause requires both - so compensation is not withheld. The SGD 6.00 charge itself reconciles with the fee schedule: the AIRPORT zone-class fee is SGD 6.00 and the RYDE_PLUS vehicle-tier fee is SGD 6.00, and the resolution rule takes the greater, so there is no fare defect under POL-NS-08(d).

On weight and escalation: the deciding facts are carried by the GPS trace, trip record, fare breakdown and driver profile, all at admissibility weight 1.0 with no issue codes, so nothing that decides this case is discounted. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09102-01 (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) is disclosed, but no surviving claim builds on it and the trace shows a single in-geofence interval, so it carries no deciding fact and does not cap confidence or trigger escalation. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: neither profile shows disputes_with_counterparty_90d (both 0), rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, the anti-farming check has not tripped, and confidence is above the 0.70 floor. The driver's counterparty statement corroborates his account of waiting at Door 5 and replying promptly, consistent with the trace and chat log. Because the ruling moves money to the driver, amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carry the same figure, SGD 4.80; the rider's charge stands as itemised. No clause in this category produces a referral on these facts.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Rider and driver: this one is decided on the arithmetic of the waiting period, and both sides agree on it.

The charge is the SGD 8.00 cancellation line on EV-FARE-09103, which is the greater of the SGD 4.00 LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee and the SGD 8.00 RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee — exactly what the fee schedule's resolution rule prescribes, so there is no fare defect and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged.

POL-NS-01 is conjunctive, and limb (c) fails. Limbs (a), (b) and (d) are made out: EV-TRIP-09103 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 17:15:20; EV-GPS-09103 places the driver about 24 m from the Plaza Singapura pin, well inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, from 17:15:00 — before the arrival event — and the trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW. But the continuous in-geofence hold runs from the first qualifying fix at 17:15:00 to the cancellation at 17:19:00: 240 seconds against the 300 seconds the schedule requires for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, a shortfall of 60 seconds. The trip record's own wait_time_min of 3.7 minutes agrees.

POL-NS-06 then governs, and it is strict liability: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the minimum, the cancellation fee is refunded in full whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. The rider's presence is not in issue and I make no finding that she was at the bay: her own track in EV-GPS-09103 sits about 519 m from the pin with no qualifying fix inside the 150 m rider-presence radius, so POL-NS-04 cannot be run in her favour — limb (a) has no rider message and limb (c) is affirmatively failed. That costs her nothing here, because the refund follows from the driver's dwell alone. I accept the driver's own candid evidence that the hold was one minute short and that the SGD 8.00 does not stand.

I accept the disclosure that the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09103-01 is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0, which can carry no fact) and that POL-NS-06(i) cannot be used to sum intervals: the trace shows a single in-geofence interval (run_count 1), so there is no second interval to add and no populated advisory that would permit it. The driver receives no compensation: POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limb (c) is not, so the 80 percent figure of SGD 6.40 does not arise. No anti-farming pattern exists (no_show_terminations_30d of 1 against a threshold of 4, and 1 in 120 completed trips), so POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged.

I have run the escalation grounds and none fires. Nothing is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d): the 'arrived' event sits on a GPS fix at that same instant (no clock skew), the trace carries 25 fixes with a maximum gap of 0 seconds across the window, the chat log holds exactly the 3 messages trip_record.chat_message_count reports, and the fare reconciles. Neither party shows a counterparty dispute in the trailing 90 days and the rider's trailing-30-day no-show dispute count is 0. The deciding fact is carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0, so confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor. The driver asked that no adverse finding or referral follow a one-minute timing defect, and none does: this clause produces no referral and no clause-mandated review instruction arises here.

Outcome: the SGD 8.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: the SGD 4.00 no-show fee charged to the rider is not chargeable and is refunded in full.

The deciding facts come from the driver's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-09104), which is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0. It places the vehicle 559.37 m from the pickup pin at Blk 180 Bukit Panjang Ring Rd (min = mean = max distance) on all 37 fixes, stationary at 0.0 km/h, with qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest in-geofence run of 0.0 seconds. The STANDARD arrival radius is 50 m and the required dwell is 300 seconds.

POL-NS-01: the fee is chargeable only if all four limbs hold. Limb (a) holds (arrival event 2026-09-04T07:25:20+08:00) and limb (d) holds (started_at null, driver-terminated at 07:31:00 with RIDER_NO_SHOW). But limb (b) fails — the trace contains no fix inside the 50 m geofence (qualifying_fix_count 0) — and limb (c) fails — measured dwell 0.0 s against the 300 s minimum, a 300-second shortfall. The conjunctive test is broken, so the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01.

POL-NS-02 independently gives the rider the full refund: there is no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the 15 minutes before the 07:31:00 cancellation, so the driver is not deemed to have arrived.

POL-NS-05 applies squarely to the arrival marker. At the 07:25:20 'arrived' timestamp the trace puts the driver 559.37 m from the pin, far beyond the clause's 300 m threshold, so the marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock. Recomputing the clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix yields none, which is POL-NS-05(ii): refund in full, no driver compensation, and the trip recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver (see referrals).

POL-NS-06 gives the same result on the 300-second shortfall, and its limb (i) accumulation cannot help the driver: there are no separate in-geofence intervals to sum (run_count 0, accumulated_sec 0.0), and the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-09104-01, is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0), so the limb's 'present and populated' requirement cannot be met.

POL-NS-03 does not rescue the fee: its entire test is a 400 m ceiling and the driver's stationary fixes sit at 559.37 m, so no wrong-entrance finding and no pin-ambiguity goodwill arise.

The driver's argument that POL-NS-09(b) requires escalation is rejected. That trigger fires only where 'no clause resolves the conflict', and POL-NS-05 resolves precisely this conflict: it treats the GPS as authoritative on position and the arrival tap as a marker that can be false. The platform system message 'Your driver has arrived' (EV-CHAT-09104, MSG-09104-001) is not an independent, contradictory account — it broadcasts the same marker the driver set — so it creates no unresolved contradiction. No other POL-NS-09 trigger fires: confidence is well above the 0.70 floor; the citable profile counters are clean (rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d 0, and disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 on both sides); and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 1 is below 4). No driver compensation is therefore payable.

Amount: EV-FARE-09104 itemises the cancellation fee at SGD 4.00 and total_charged SGD 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) agree, and the resolution rule's GREATER is SGD 4.00; the fare line reconciles, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect. The rider is refunded SGD 4.00. Confidence is 0.95, capped at 1.0 by the weight-1.0 artifacts (GPS trace and trip record) that carry the deciding facts.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii): record trip TRP-09104 as a false-arrival event against driver DRV-09104.

ruling.explanation:
This dispute over the SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee on trip TRP-09105 is decided on the GPS trace (EV-GPS-09105) and the trip record (EV-TRIP-09105), both at full weight 1.0, and the outcome is a full refund to the rider.

The fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01. Limb (b) requires the driver to be inside the pickup geofence at or before the 'arrived' event, and the arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup (NEX Serangoon, Tower B ride-hail pickup) is 120 m under the fee schedule. The driver's trace holds 34 fixes from 13:05:00 to 13:10:30, every one stationary at 0.0 km/h and 219.77 m from the pickup pin — about 100 m outside the radius — with 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds. Limb (c) fails with it: the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second minimum for LARGE_VENUE. Both advocates accept this, and POL-NS-06 confirms the full refund of the 4.00 SGD cancellation_fee line actually charged at 13:10:32.

The case is therefore the wrong-entrance case governed by POL-NS-03. The driver was stationary for the required dwell — 330 seconds, 13:05:00 to 13:10:30 — at a point outside the 120 m arrival radius but well within the clause's 400 m ceiling (219.77 m), so the fee is refunded to the rider in full. No venue-identity inference is needed or made: the 400 m distance test decides from coordinates alone.

On fault allocation, POL-NS-03 limb (i) applies, so the driver receives no compensation. The rider named the sub-location in the chat log ('I am at Tower B ride-hail pickup, beside the blue sign.' at 13:05:05; 'That is the other entrance. Please come to Tower B.' at 13:06:35), and the driver, who answered at 13:06:00 that he was 'waiting at the mall taxi stand', never moved from his fixed 219.77 m point before cancelling at 13:10:30. Limb (ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill does not apply because the rider did specify the sub-location, notwithstanding the 3 registered pickup points. The POL-NS-07 figure of SGD 3.20 (80 percent of SGD 4.00) therefore does not arise, since POL-NS-01 is not satisfied and POL-NS-03 displaces it; the anti-farming check would not trip in any event (no_show_terminations_30d 1 against completed_trips_30d 120, a rate of 0.008, against thresholds of 4 and 0.08).

The rider's POL-NS-04 claims are noted but do not change the result. The rider's messages are locating content (limb (a)) and the rider's track shows all 16 qualifying fixes about 25.01 m from the pin, inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius (limb (c)). Whether limb (b) is satisfied is left unresolved — the driver replied at 13:06:00, 55 seconds after the 13:05:05 message, though nothing after 13:06:35 — but the refund follows from POL-NS-03 either way.

No false-arrival referral is warranted. POL-NS-05 is not engaged: at the 13:05:20 arrival marker the driver was 219.77 m from the pin, inside the clause's own 300 m carve-out, and stationary at 0.0 km/h, so the marker cannot be false and no POL-NS-05(ii) record is produced. The empty referrals list reflects that no clause produces one here.

No escalation. POL-NS-08 does not apply: there is no clock skew (the 13:05:20 arrival event lands on a fix timestamp and the 13:10:30 cancellation matches the last fix), no trace gap (max_gap_sec 0.0, 34 fixes, well above the 6-fix floor), the chat log's 4 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 4 with no msg_id gap, and the 4.00 SGD cancellation fee equals the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00) under the resolution rule, so there is no limb (d) defect. Neither POL-NS-09(a) (confidence is above the 0.70 floor) nor limbs (b) to (e) fires; rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0 and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0.

Amounts: SGD 4.00 is refunded out of the SGD 4.00 charged (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). Driver compensation is nil.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Rider and driver, you agree on the physical facts, and they are these. The driver reached the Tampines MRT Exit D private-hire bay at 18:20:20 on 6 September 2026, and the GPS trace shows his vehicle holding position 24.0 m from the pickup pin in one continuous run of 330 seconds, from 18:20:00 to 18:25:30, at 0 km/h throughout. He cancelled at 18:25:30 on reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. On the Driver Advocate's POL-NS-01 case all four limbs hold and I accept each of them: the trip record carries the arrived event (a); the trace puts him inside the 150 m TRANSPORT_HUB arrival radius before it (b); he held 330 seconds against the 300 second minimum (c); and the trip ended by the driver on a recognised code after the dwell elapsed (d). I also accept the driver's POL-NS-05 point — 24.0 m at 0 km/h is nowhere near the 300 m or 15 km/h triggers, so the arrival marker is genuine — and the rider's own concession that POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to refund on. Nothing turns on those: they clear the baseline clause rather than decide the case. POL-NS-01 charges the fee only where no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-04 does. The chat log shows two locating messages from the rider inside the waiting window — 'I am at Exit D under the green sign. Where is your car?' at 18:21:00 and 'I still cannot see you. Please reply.' at 18:23:25 — and the driver answered neither: the 18:21:00 message was read at 18:21:15 and left unanswered past the 120 second window, and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so no voice call was placed either. That is limbs (a) and (b). Limb (c) is met too: the rider's device sits 41.9 m from the pin on all 16 of her 16 qualifying fixes, well inside the 200 m presence radius for a transport hub, so this is the satisfied case and not the undecidable one. All three limbs hold, and POL-NS-04 refunds the cancellation fee in full with no driver compensation payable. That disposes of the driver's POL-NS-07 claim for SGD 4.80: compensation is payable under that clause only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied and undisplaced, and POL-NS-04 displaces it. I reject the SGD 4.80 on that ground and not on any anti-farming finding — the check does not trip, since 1 no-show termination in 30 days is below the threshold of 4 and 1/120 = 0.008 is below 0.08. The driver's counter-statement that he 'waited inside the station pickup geofence until the timer ended' confirms his presence and says nothing about having replied, and POL-NS-03 is not engaged either, because he was inside the arrival radius, so no pin-ambiguity goodwill arises. Amount: fare_breakdown shows the cancellation-fee line at SGD 6.00, total_charged 6.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so SGD 6.00 is what the rider is presently carrying and SGD 6.00 is what is returned to her. No escalation and no referral. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact is admitted COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the POL-NS-08 limbs are not engaged and confidence is not capped below 1.0: the fee reconciles with the fee schedule (TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee 6.00 and RYDE_PLUS vehicle-tier fee 6.00 tie, so the greater, 6.00, governs), there is no clock skew, no sampling gap (max gap 0.0 s across 34 fixes), and the chat log is complete at 3 of 3 messages. The single MISSING artifact, EV-ADVIS-09106-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), is not relied on by this ruling — no traffic advisory is needed because the dwell was never short — so it neither lowers confidence nor triggers anything. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires, and no clause produces a referral: POL-NS-05(ii) is not engaged because qualifying in-geofence fixes exist, and POL-NS-07's anti-farming branch does not trip. On the profiles, I have read no lifetime counter or rating against the rider: prior_no_show_flags and prior_disputes_filed are context only, and the trailing-window fields that could bear on escalation (0 no-show disputes in 30 days, 0 disputes with this driver on either side) do not.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: on the driving facts this was a genuine, verified no-show, but the driver's own profile trips the anti-farming check, so the case cannot be paid out and must go to a human reviewer. The disputed amount (SGD 4.00) is held, not collected and not refunded, until that review finishes.

Why the fee is valid on the merits (POL-NS-01). All four limbs hold. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-08T09:30:20. (b) The GPS trace places the driver 24.0 m from the pickup pin, well inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, from the first fix at 09:30:00 — before the arrived event. (c) The trace shows one continuous qualifying in-geofence run of 330 seconds, measured from the first in-geofence fix (09:30:00), against the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum — 30 seconds over, not under (shortfall_sec -30.0). (d) The driver terminated the trip at 09:35:30 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the dwell elapsed at 09:35:00.

The displacing clauses do not fire. POL-NS-02 confirms arrival (34 qualifying in-geofence fixes, no clock-skew issue). POL-NS-03 is about a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m; here the driver was inside the radius at 24.0 m, so the wrong-entrance route is not engaged. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider: limb (a) fails because the chat log holds only the SYSTEM arrival notice and the driver's own 'Waiting at PLQ 3 pickup bay', nothing locating or coordinating from the rider, and limb (c) fails affirmatively — the rider track's 16 fixes sit at a mean 519 m from the pin, outside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius, with 0 qualifying fixes. POL-NS-05 does not bite: at the arrived timestamp the driver was 24.0 m from the pin (not over 300 m) and the trace records a single distinct speed of 0.0 km/h (not 15 km/h or more), so the arrival marker is genuine. POL-NS-06 does not apply: the effective dwell of 330 seconds exceeds the 300-second minimum, and its limb (i) could not be run in any case because the only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09108-01) is MISSING, weight 0.0, and can carry no fact under POL-GEN-02.

The amount is correct. Under fee_schedule.resolution_rule the chargeable fee is the GREATER of the zone-class fee (LARGE_VENUE, SGD 4.00) and the vehicle-tier fee (RYDE_X, SGD 4.00), i.e. SGD 4.00, which is exactly the cancellation_fee line in the fare breakdown; there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect.

Why the outcome is ESCALATE, not a driver payout. POL-NS-07 would pay the driver 80 percent of the fee, SGD 3.20 of SGD 4.00 — but compensation is subject to the anti-farming check, and both its conjunctive limbs are met on driver_profile: no_show_terminations_30d is 7 (4 or more) and 7 divided by completed_trips_30d of 70 is 0.10, greater than 0.08. Compensation is therefore withheld and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d). The two driver-advocate claims that the withholding and the hold apply are accepted; the same claim's further assertion that the rider's refund demand is 'still refused at the pipeline level' is rejected — on escalation the fee is held, and POL-NS-07 directs the escalation packet to instruct the reviewer to refund the rider's SGD 4.00 in full, which is exactly what the rider's advocate argued and what the single referral records. The rider's claim that POL-NS-06 offers no relief on this trace is accepted, as is the rider's point that the abuse indicators here all run driver-side: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 (limb (d) needs 3 or more), and rider_profile and driver_profile disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so limb (c) is not met either. Under POL-GEN-01 the rider's lifetime prior_no_show_flags (1) is context only and carries no adverse finding; it was flagged for context and used for nothing.

Confidence is 0.95. Every artifact that carries a deciding fact here — the GPS trace, the trip record, the fare breakdown and the driver profile — sits at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0; the only impaired item (the missing advisory, weight 0.0) decides nothing. The escalation is compelled by POL-NS-07/POL-NS-09(d), not by the confidence floor of 0.70.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-07: instruct the human reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee of SGD 4.00 in full; pending that review the fee is held and is neither collected nor refunded by the automated pipeline.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties.

OUTCOME. The SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee stands (the charge is not refunded), and the driver is paid SGD 3.20 as compensation. The figure is read off the fare breakdown and POL-NS-07: 80% of the SGD 4.00 fee = SGD 3.20.

DRIVER'S CASE. POL-NS-01 is satisfied in all four limbs. (a) EV-TRIP-09107 records a driver 'arrived' event at 19:00:20. (b) EV-GPS-09107 places the driver inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, 35 of 40 fixes qualifying, with the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 19:00:00 — before the arrival event. (c) The effective in-geofence dwell is 330 seconds against the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum. (d) No boarding event is recorded and the driver terminated at 19:06:30 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the dwell had elapsed. No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces the fee.

THE RIDER'S CENTRAL ARGUMENT — that the car left the bay so the two waits cannot be added together. This is the point on which the case turns, and it is answered on the face of POL-NS-06(i). That limb expressly permits separate in-geofence intervals within a single pickup attempt to be accumulated where the driver never travelled more than 300 m from the pin AND a qualifying traffic advisory covers the pickup road during the waiting period. Both conditions hold: EV-ADVIS-09107-01 is a CLOSURE, present and populated, its geometry covers the pickup road and its active window (18:50–19:30) covers the wait; and the driver's furthest point between the intervals was 179.76 m, inside the 300 m leash. The trace is a 170-second hold (19:00:00–19:02:50), a 60-second circulation taken to 179.76 m, and a 160-second hold (19:03:50–19:06:30): 330 seconds in total, 30 seconds above the 300-second minimum. The separate waits therefore do count together, and the fee is chargeable. Your assertion that the longest unbroken run is only 170 seconds is correct as a fact but does not decide the limb, because POL-NS-06(i) supplies the accumulation rule.

Your further point that the trip record's wait_time_min of 6.2 is not the measure POL-NS-01 limb (c) prescribes is accepted — the measure is the GPS-derived in-geofence dwell — but on the correct measure the wait still clears the minimum. Your point that POL-NS-06 decides the refund on the dwell computation 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded' is also accepted; there is simply no shortfall on that computation.

OTHER CLAUSES. POL-NS-04 does not apply: no message in EV-CHAT-09107 was sent by the rider, so limb (a) fails and the clause is never reached. POL-NS-03 does not apply: the driver was inside the arrival radius, not outside it but within 400 m. POL-NS-05 is not triggered: at the arrival timestamp 19:00:20 the driver was inside the 120 m radius, far short of that clause's 300 m threshold, so the arrival marker is not false. The rider-track figure of 519.37 m and the absence of any rider chat message do not assist either party here, because POL-NS-06 directs the dwell question to be decided independently of rider presence.

DRIVER COMPENSATION. POL-NS-07 pays the driver because POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it: 80% of the SGD 4.00 fee = SGD 3.20. The anti-farming check does not trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below the threshold of 4) and 1 divided by 120 completed trips in 30 days is 0.008 (below 0.08) — so compensation is paid rather than withheld. The disposition of the SGD 4.00 fee itself is NO_ACTION: the rider's charge stands as it is.

CONFIDENCE AND ESCALATION. No POL-NS-08 impairment applies — no clock skew (the arrival event and nearest fix coincide within seconds), no sampling gap (max gap 0.0 s, 40 fixes), the chat log's 3 entries match trip_record.chat_message_count and its msg_id sequence is unbroken, and the SGD 4.00 fee reconciles with the fee_schedule resolution rule (greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee SGD 4.00). No POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged. Confidence 0.90, capped by the deciding artifacts, all at weight 1.0. The profile figures cited are within the fields POL-GEN-01 permits (POL-NS-07 and POL-NS-09 counters); every other profile field is context only and carried no weight in this decision.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: this case is sent to a human reviewer, and no money moves while that review is pending. The trip-level facts are not really in dispute. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-09110) shows the driver holding position about 24 m from the pickup pin — well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — for one unbroken 330-second stretch from 06:50:00 to 06:55:30 at 0 km/h, which is 30 seconds more than the 300-second minimum wait for a STANDARD pickup. The trip record (EV-TRIP-09110) shows the 'arrived' event at 06:50:20 and the driver ending the trip at 06:55:30 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event. On the merits that would carry POL-NS-01 in full and would pay the driver SGD 3.20 under POL-NS-07 — 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee itemised in EV-FARE-09110 — the anti-farming guard not being tripped (1 no-show termination in the last 30 days, below 4; 1 divided by 120 completed trips = 0.008, below 0.08). The rider's routes do not change that on the merits: POL-NS-04 cannot run because the driver replied 'Okay, waiting.' at 06:52:00, only 20 seconds after the rider's 06:51:40 message, inside the 120-second window, so limb (b) fails, and the rider's own device sat about 519 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, so limb (c) fails too; POL-NS-05 does not apply because the arrival marker matches a stationary fix 24 m from the pin, not 300 m or 15 km/h; POL-NS-06 does not apply because the hold was 330 seconds, above the 300-second minimum. What stops the automated ruling is POL-NS-09(c): both profiles (EV-RPROF-09110 and EV-DPROF-09110) record disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2, i.e. two no-show disputes between this same rider and this same driver in the trailing 90 days, which is '2 or more' and is a mandatory escalation trigger — exactly the repeat pattern the rider's own words, 'another dispute with the same driver', describe. Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and under POL-GEN-03 replaces any monetary ruling, so no refund and no compensation issue here and the SGD 4.00 fee is held rather than collected or refunded; the fare breakdown shows it at payment_status PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. This is neither a rider win nor a driver loss. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0); nothing rests on it, because the 330-second hold is a single continuous in-geofence run, so no accumulation of separate intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is needed. The driver's prior_no_show_flags lifetime figure of 2 is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used to build any adverse finding; only the trailing-window counters the clauses name were read. Open question for the reviewer: whether this pair's repeated no-show disputes reflect a genuine rider no-show on this trip or a recurring pickup-point or pin problem between this rider and this driver at Blk 612 Bedok Reservoir Road. Confidence 0.9, capped by the profile artifacts at weight 1.0 that carry the escalation facts.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: this case goes to a human reviewer, and the SGD 6.00 cancellation fee is held — neither collected nor refunded — until that review is done.

What the record shows is not in dispute. The trip record (EV-TRIP-09109, weight 1.0) shows the driver marked 'arrived' at 21:10:20 on 9 Sep, the trip was then cancelled by the driver at 21:15:40 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, an interval of 5.3 minutes. The chat log (EV-CHAT-09109, weight 1.0) shows the driver writing 'I am at the private-hire bay' at 21:10:40 and 'I am here beside the sign' at 21:11:45, and the rider writing 'I am at the bay and cannot see your car' at 21:11:30. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-09109, weight 1.0) shows a cancellation fee of SGD 6.00, and that arithmetic is correct: it is the greater of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), with payment_status PENDING and refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

The difficulty is that the one thing that could settle the dispute is not in the file. A no-show fee stands only if all four POL-NS-01 limbs hold, and two of them are about the driver's GPS position: limb (b) needs the GPS trace to put the driver inside the 150 m arrival radius at the Woodlands MRT private-hire bay at or before 21:10:20, and limb (c) measures the 300-second continuous dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, expressly not from the arrival tap. The only GPS artifact, EV-GPS-09109, is MISSING — no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — and the driver's own statement concedes 'the GPS export is unavailable.'

That absence cuts both ways, which is why no monetary ruling issues. A trace that does not exist is not a trace showing the driver was elsewhere, so I do not accept the rider's argument that the fee must be refunded in full: the absence of readings is the limiting case of an impaired stretch, and POL-NS-02 itself treats a trace too sparse to establish the required readings as impaired under POL-NS-08(b) rather than as proof the driver never arrived. Limbs (b) and (c) are accordingly undecided — they support neither the fee (which needs them to hold) nor the refund (which needs them to fail). Equally, the driver's request for SGD 4.80 compensation under POL-NS-07 is refused because that clause pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, which it is not; the anti-farming check (no_show_terminations_30d of 1, and 1 ÷ 120 = 0.008) is not the reason it fails.

The rider's POL-NS-04 route does not open, and the driver is right on that point: the driver answered the rider's 21:11:30 message at 21:11:45, fifteen seconds later and well inside the 120-second window, so limb (b) of that clause fails irrespective of the reply's content. The false-arrival test (POL-NS-05) and the waiting-period shortfall test (POL-NS-06) cannot be run either, both needing the GPS fixes that do not exist, and the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09109-01 is likewise MISSING. No fare defect arises to discount the charge (POL-NS-08(d)).

Because the only evidence that could carry the deciding fact is the missing GPS trace at weight 0.0, POL-NS-08 and POL-NS-09(e) send this to a human reviewer, and POL-NS-09(a) is met as well, since this record can support no confidence at or above the 0.70 floor. Escalation is terminal, so no money moves and no referral issues — no clause directs one here: POL-NS-05(ii)'s false-arrival record needs a trace showing no qualifying fix, which cannot be shown where no trace exists, and POL-NS-07's instruction to refund the fee applies only when its anti-farming test trips, which it does not. The open question for the reviewer, and it belongs in the explanation rather than a referral, is whether the driver was in fact inside the Woodlands MRT private-hire bay from 21:10:20 and held position there for the full 300 seconds; the disputed SGD 6.00 stays on hold while that is settled.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both of you: this dispute turns entirely on the route-deviation threshold in POL-RD-01, and on that test the claim does not succeed.

THE MEASUREMENT. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure, and the trip_record's actual_distance_km a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test. The trace (EV-GPS-09112) reads 11.5 km; the booking-time optimal route stored on the trip record (EV-TRIP-09112) is 10.0 km. The excess is 1.5 km, or 15.00% of the optimal distance.

THE TEST. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km. The 1.5 km excess clears the absolute limb (0.8 km) but fails the percentage limb: 15.00% is below 20%. Both limbs must pass, and the clause says in terms that if either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The deviation is therefore not established on this trip.

RIDER. Your submission that the 1.5 km is real and measured on an unimpaired trace is accepted: the trace carries 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07 and POL-GEN-02 gives no discount. But a real, unimpaired excess that does not clear both threshold limbs is simply not a deviation under this policy, and your own final submission concedes the percentage limb is short.

Your conditional POL-RD-02 arithmetic (recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 10.0 + 0.28 x 20.0) x surge 1.0, read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 = 17.70; refund = 19.39 charged_total - 17.70 = 1.69, rounded up to 1.70) is answered but does not run: POL-RD-02 applies only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, and it is not. Your alternative request to hold the SGD 1.69 for a human reviewer under POL-RD-10 is refused because no POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all match TRP-09112; the trace is not impaired; the timestamps agree; and there is no admissible contradictory evidence of comparable strength between the parties. The billing-integrity route under POL-RD-09(4) is also closed on this record: erp_gantries is empty, tolls/ERP are 0.00, and the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no phantom line to refund in full.

DRIVER. Your counter-statement that you 'stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop' cites no evidence ID and carries no weight under POL-RD-08; it is not relied on, and the ruling does not need it. The traffic-advisory slot EV-ADVIS-09112-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), so no closure exoneration under POL-RD-03 was available to you either — but since no deviation is established, none is needed.

OUTCOME. The rider's claim is not supported by the evidence at the threshold the policy sets, so the present state stands: payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 are left as they are, and the SGD 1.69 is neither refunded nor held. No clause produces a referral here: POL-RD-06(c) is not engaged (there is no MATERIAL deviation and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days), and there is no billing-integrity finding under POL-RD-09(4).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both parties: the booked optimal route for TRP-09111 is 12.0 km. The GPS trace — the governing field under POL-RD-01 — records 16.2 km driven, an excess of 4.2 km, or 35.0%. That clears both establishment tests (over 20% of optimal and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence. It does not clear the materiality tests (over 50% or over 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610, reaching neither the 3-flag count nor the 0.05 ratio, so there is no repeat-deviation pattern, no uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The trace is clean (205 fixes, 10-second interval, max_gap_sec 0, no gaps), so POL-RD-07 imposes no corroboration requirement and the excess is measured on the trace itself.

No exculpatory clause applies. POL-RD-03 is not run: the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-09111-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0, and the driver does not press a closure. POL-RD-04 fails — the chat log holds no rider instruction carrying a waypoint_hint or naming a road, and the rider's own message asked the driver to return to the booked route. POL-RD-05 fails — neither endpoint was amended. POL-RD-12 fails — vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL.

The fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs. Charged_total of 33.36 less the recomputed fare of 24.2240 — ((3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min) x the 1.2 surge multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown, + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal ERP - 1.00 promo discount) — gives 9.1360, rounded UP to SGD 9.15. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15, which is the contested amount.

The 2.00 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' ERP line is NOT added on top: the recomputed fare already credits only the 1.00 on-optimal Pioneer Road gantry, so the 2.00 is returned inside the 9.15 (POL-RD-09(1)) and adding it again would be the double count that limb forbids. Separately, that gantry is one the trace never passes — its nearest fix is 1,645.7 m away, outside the 250 m match radius — and it has no counterpart on the trip_record, so under POL-RD-09(4) it is a billing-integrity finding and is recorded as a referral; because it is refunded under that limb, POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged and no escalation arises. The 1.00 Pioneer Road inbound line lies on the optimal route and is correctly retained. Both profiles were used as credibility weighting only (POL-GEN-01); no adverse finding rests on rating, lifetime counters or any other context-only field. Confidence 0.90: every artifact that carries the deciding facts (trace, trip record, fare breakdown) sits at weight 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity — the SGD 2.00 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' ERP charge is for a gantry the GPS trace never passes (nearest fix 1,645.7 m, far outside the 250 m match radius) and has no counterpart on the trip_record; the amount is returned inside the POL-RD-02 recomputation and the line is recorded here as a billing-integrity finding.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver — TRP-09113, rider-filed. Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND — SGD 9.05 of the SGD 31.42 charged is returned to the rider.

Deviation established (POL-RD-01, POL-RD-08, POL-RD-07). The governing measurement is the GPS trace, 18.0 km, against the booking-time optimal of 10.0 km: an excess of 8.0 km and 80%, clearing both POL-RD-01 gates (>20% and >0.8 km) and amounting to a MATERIAL deviation. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes — 205 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, maximum gap 0 s — so no POL-RD-07(a)–(c) limb fires and the POL-RD-10(3) route is not open. The rider's POL-RD-08 burden is discharged: trip identifiers and pickup timestamps match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown.

Closure cap (POL-RD-03) — accepted from both sides. LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 names the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, which the booked optimal route traverses, and its 18:14–18:55 window brackets the trip. Justified excess = min(8.0, 1.30 × (12.0 − 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km; closure-adjusted optimal = 13.60 km / 27.2 min.

Deviation refund (POL-RD-02). charged_total = 31.42. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 13.60 + 0.28 × 27.2) × 1.0, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP = 23.416. Refund = 31.42 − 23.416 = 8.004, i.e. 8.05. That is 25.5% of charged_total — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and below the 90% full-refund share — so a partial refund, not a full one.

ERP (POL-RD-09). The 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' line is off-route (nearest fix 223 m) and is already comprehended in the 8.05 under POL-RD-09(1); it is itemised but never added. The 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' line is where I part from both advocates: its nearest trace fix is 834.18 m, far outside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 uses, so the trace never crosses it. Under POL-RD-09(4) it is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, and it does not engage POL-RD-10(8), which that limb expressly excludes where the only unmatched line is refunded under it. Total refund = 8.004 + 1.00 = 9.004, rounded up to SGD 9.05.

No escalation (POL-RD-10). No trigger fires: identifiers match, the trace is clean, timestamps agree, the advisory is present and covers the trip window, and 9.004 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total. The rider's assertion that both ERP gantries lie within the 250 m radius is rejected on its own figures — the 834 m it cites is outside it — but the disposal is unchanged, because an unmatched line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), not escalated.

No POL-RD-04 exoneration and no driver compensation. The rider's only message names no road and carries waypoint_hint null, so the corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable; the industrial-loop distance is therefore not excluded, and the rider's authorisation does not reduce the excess. There is no billing shortfall (18.0 km billed against 18.0 km recorded), so the compensation limb does not arise.

No conduct uplift and no conduct referral. The POL-RD-06 check runs because the deviation is MATERIAL, but finds no pattern: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610 — neither limb met. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) referral. Only those two citable fields were used; the rest of either profile is context only under POL-GEN-01.

Confidence 0.9. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — GPS trace, trip record, fare breakdown and LTA advisory — is at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and nothing rests on a discounted artifact.

The one clause-mandated referral is listed above. For the human reviewer, the open question (which belongs here, not in the referrals list) is whether the Pelton gantry charge is a one-off mislocation or a systemic phantom-line defect.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity — the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' ERP line (lat 1.33, lng 103.883) is unmatched to the GPS trace (nearest fix 834.18 m, outside the 250 m match radius); it has been refunded in full as a standalone correction and is referred for a billing-integrity review of that gantry charge.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 3.20 you are disputing (rider) and the SGD 3.20 you accept is owed (driver) is the same figure, and the record confirms it. Here is the reasoning.

What happened. This was an upfront-quoted trip. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-09114) records quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 22.00 and a charged_total of SGD 25.20. The whole SGD 3.20 gap between those two figures is the single ERP line, 'Bukit Merah Central westbound', charged at SGD 3.20. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-09114) is complete: 169 fixes, 100% coverage, a 10-second sampling interval and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. Its derived ERP proximity check places the vehicle's nearest fix 7,482.07 m from that gantry's coordinates. POL-RD-09 treats a gantry as crossed only where a fix comes within 250 m; 7,482 m is about thirty times that radius, and the derived block reports gap_brackets_closest_approach false with no bracketing gaps. On any reading the car did not pass this gantry. The driver's own statement on file — that he 'did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt' — is a concession against his own interest and points the same way; it carries no weight_multiplier, so it does not move the confidence cap, but it is consistent with the instruments rather than contradicting them.

The deviation. The trace measures 16.0 km against a 12.5 km optimal route, an excess of 3.5 km or 28.0%. That clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km) but not its materiality gate (over 50% or over 8.0 km), so this is not a MATERIAL deviation. POL-RD-06's driver-profile check is therefore never engaged, and in any event the profile shows 0 deviation flags in 90 days against 610 completed trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established. Because the fare model is UPFRONT_QUOTE, POL-RD-11 governs: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess — the driver bears the unrecovered detour cost on an upfront trip. I accept that part of both submissions.

The refund. That leaves the pass-through line. charged_total (SGD 25.20) less quoted_fare (SGD 22.00) is SGD 3.20, and the only line making up that gap is the ERP charge, which was not properly chargeable because the gantry was never crossed. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge for a gantry the trace never passes is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The rider's recovery is therefore the whole SGD 3.20 — which is the whole of the contested amount — and under POL-GEN-03 a filing party who is entirely right on the contested sum and has all of it returned is recorded as FULL_REFUND, not a partial winner. The amount is SGD 3.20, already a multiple of SGD 0.05.

No escalation, no conduct referral, no driver compensation. POL-RD-10 is not engaged: the only unmatched charge line is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-09 expressly excludes from the POL-RD-10(8) trigger; the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown (TRP-09114); the trace is unimpaired; the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling; and the deciding artifacts sit at weight 1.0, above the 0.70 floor. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09114-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries no fact in this ruling — it is cited only to show that no closure exoneration under POL-RD-03 is available — so no escalation turns on it. No POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral attaches, because there is no material deviation and no pattern; the driver has done nothing here beyond a bookkeeping error, and the driver's submission that this is a fare-correction matter rather than a conduct one is accepted. No driver compensation is due: distance_charged_km (16.0) matches the trace distance (16.0), so there is no unbilled shortfall under POL-RD-04.

Confidence. The deciding fact — that the gantry was never crossed and the SGD 3.20 line was not chargeable — is carried by the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, both at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0 and I set confidence at 0.95. The referral under POL-RD-09(4) rides with this money ruling and does not displace it; the disputed SGD 3.20 is refunded to the rider, and nothing further is owed in either direction.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) — billing-integrity finding: the SGD 3.20 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' ERP line on EV-FARE-09114 was charged for a gantry the GPS trace (EV-GPS-09114) never crosses — the nearest fix is 7,482 m from the gantry coordinates against the 250 m match radius, with no bracketing gaps — and the line has been refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction.

the claim cites impaired artifact EV-GPS-09115 at weight_multiplier 0.6 but does not name its issue code(s): GPS_GAP

ruling.explanation:
Both parties — this case goes to a human reviewer. No money moves: the disputed SGD 5.80 is held rather than collected or refunded, because the evidence cannot answer the question the dispute turns on.

WHY. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-09115) is impaired at two levels, and both should be said out loud. At the schema level the admissibility pre-pass tags it IMPAIRED with weight_multiplier 0.6 and issue code GPS_GAP. At the policy level it also meets POL-RD-07(a): it contains a 160-second gap between consecutive fixes, from 20:03:10 to 20:05:50, falling inside the very segment the rider disputes — well over the 90-second limit. Where a trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c), POL-RD-07(ii) says a deviation may NOT be established on the trace alone; it needs an independent source from the closed list of four.

We went through all four, and none is present:
• No driver admission in the chat log (EV-CHAT-09115): the rider writes that the route display jumped away from the booked road; the driver replies only that his own navigation display refreshed and he continued toward the destination.
• No charged ERP gantry on the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-09115): erp_gantries is empty and tolls_erp is 0.00, so no gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use.
• No admission in the driver's statement: it denies any extra stop or detour request, and it cannot account for the telemetry gap.
• No independently derived distance: trip_record.actual_distance_km is 15.0 km, identical to gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 15.0 km and to distance_charged_km of 15.0 km. POL-RD-01 itself describes actual_distance_km as a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement, so it is a copy of the trace, not an independent source.

Because the trace is impaired and nothing independent corroborates it, the rider's threshold showing under POL-RD-08(b) is not made, and POL-RD-07(iii) directs ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION — the absence of proof here is a data failure, not a finding for the driver. POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory and terminal. Confidence is capped at 0.6, the weight of the impaired trace that carries the deciding fact, which is below the 0.70 floor; POL-RD-10(1) points the same way.

ON THE MONEY CLAIMS. The rider asked for SGD 5.80, and the arithmetic is correct on its face: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75×11.0 + 0.28×22.0) × 1.1 + 0.80, where the 1.1 multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-09115 and nowhere else = 18.21 × 1.1 + 0.80 = 20.831; charged_total 26.60 − 20.831 = 5.769, rounded UP to SGD 5.80. But POL-RD-02 runs only where a deviation is established, and here it cannot be established on an impaired, uncorroborated trace, so no distance-or-time refund is available and the fare stays as charged. The driver's point that the excess (4.0 km, 36.4%) sits below both the 50% and the 8.0 km materiality gate is accepted: no MATERIAL deviation is recorded, no POL-RD-06(b) uplift is available, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days establishes no repeat pattern — so no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral either.

EXCULPATORY CLAUSES change nothing. No traffic advisory was available (EV-ADVIS-09115-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot exonerate anyone; the chat log carries no rider detour instruction and both waypoint_hint fields are null, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable on this record; the trip record shows no amendment (pickup/dropoff amendment fields and amended_optimal_distance_km all null) and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 have no application.

BILLING INTEGRITY produces no referral: erp_gantries is empty, airport_surcharge is 0.00, there is no charge line without a counterpart, and the fare is METERED and CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0 — POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged. The counterparty statement carries no weight_multiplier and so enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the confidence cap.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT: an unimpaired trace across the disputed stretch, or one of the four POL-RD-07(ii) sources — a driver admission, a charged gantry placing the vehicle off the optimal corridor, a counterparty admission of the route, or a distance figure the platform derived independently of this trace.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
